title: Characterization of 9-12% Cr Tempered Martensite Ferritic Steels using Correlative Multi-Modal Scanning Electron Microscopy
content: Tempered martensite ferritic (TMF) steels with 9–12% Cr are extensively used for high-temperature steam pipes, turbines, and boilers in electrical power plants. The TMF steel structure consists of a hierarchical arrangement of prior-austenite grains (PAG), packets, blocks, and micrograins with a high density of free dislocations. During in-service creep conditions, the microstructure evolves due to changes in secondary phases, grain boundaries, and dislocation structures, leading to a decrease in creep resistance over time [1]. Quantitative measurements of this microstructural evolution on samples subjected to long-term interrupted creep testing can validate physics-based creep-rupture prediction models [2]. Microstructural studies on these alloys are typically performed on extraction replicas or electropolished thin foils using TEM-based techniques (SAED, EFTEM, STEM-EDS/EELS) [1]. However, these analyses are time-consuming and limited to electron-transparent areas of the thin foil.
